about: Halabi's phone symbols of the Arabic Speech Corpus TextGrids, mapped to IPA, with the source of each. Read on Nov 10, 2026. Used by ArabicSpeechCorpus.py.

sources.T47R: Halabi 2016 thesis, Table 4-7, 'Phonemes Revisited' rows, section 4.4, about p. 46, read through a text extraction of the PDF (not checked on the rendered page). The vowel rows are not confirmed, see the note on a
sources.LREC: Halabi and Wald 2016, LREC, 'Phonetic inventory for an Arabic speech corpus', Table 1, section 4.1, read through a text extraction of the PDF
sources.R5.1: Halabi 2016 thesis, section 5.1, p. 52, phonetisation rules, read through a text extraction of the PDF
sources.BROSELOW: Broselow, E., Arabic syllable structure, Stony Brook University, https://linguistics.stonybrook.edu/faculty/ellen.broselow/files/Broselow_ArabicSyllStrPaper_revised.pdf
sources.SITE: the corpus site's text on stress marks, as copied at https://dagshub.com/DagsHub/audio-datasets/src/main/Arabic-Speech-Corpus

rules.silence: sil is a pause (README, and rule 4 of section 5.1). It is no phone, and its timestamps carry an empty string
rules.gemination: a doubled consonant symbol is a geminate (thesis Table 4-7 text). It is written with the IPA length mark
rules.stress: an apostrophe after a vowel marks a stressed syllable (SITE). In the IPA string, ˈ goes before the one consonant that starts that syllable, since a syllable of Modern Standard Arabic starts with exactly one consonant (BROSELOW), or before the vowel after a pause. Before a geminate it goes before the whole geminate. The timestamps carry no stress

<.note: rule 7 writes the glottal stop as /</

j.note: the thesis table lists both ʒ and d͡ʒ for this letter. LREC Table 1 gives j as ʒ and J as d͡ʒ

g.note: the thesis table writes this letter as G. The corpus writes it as g, as LREC Table 1 and rule 8 of section 5.1 do

a.note: the extracted table gives a for a but æː for aa, while every other short and long pair has the same quality. The extraction may have shifted the IPA column, so a may be æ. Kept as extracted. For Alex

u0.note: the extracted table prints æ for u0, but its own Arabic column for u0 is the damma, and uu0 is uː. u is used. For Alex

I0.note: capital letter marks a vowel next to an emphatic consonant (rule 8). The thesis gives no IPA of its own, so the lower case vowel is used. For Alex

-.note: the README marks the schwa as '-'

no_ipa.dist: the README says corrupt phonemes are marked dist. No phone
no_ipa.G: the thesis table gives G as ɣ, but the corpus writes ɣ as g. G is in 3 words, such as the Yangtze river, so its sound is not known
no_ipa.AH: in no table of the thesis or the LREC paper
no_ipa.Ah: in no table of the thesis or the LREC paper
no_ipa.u: a u with no 0 or 1. In no table of the thesis
